summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for severe neck and throat pain, tachycardia, and a productive cough, in the setting of ongoing treatment for tracheal squamous cell carcinoma. She was found to have candidal esophagitis, likely exacerbated by recent radiation and chemotherapy, contributing to dysphagia and pain. A bloodstream infection due to her central venous catheter was identified, with Staphylococcus isolated from blood cultures, prompting antibiotic therapy and PICC line replacement. She also had acute bronchitis and chronic obstructive asthma exacerbation, though imaging showed no pneumonia. Malnutrition and edema were managed with TPN and nutritional support. Her tachycardia improved with metoprolol. Over the 12-day admission, she transitioned from TPN to oral intake, completed antibiotic treatment, and showed clinical improvement. She was discharged home with home health services, a revised medication plan, and follow-up with oncology.
